function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

messages.content:
"""SQL statement report builder.

The analytics intake pipeline lets external clients submit raw SQL batches for
static analysis; this module parses a submitted batch with sqlparse and emits a
statement-level statistics report. The SQL text is client-controlled input, so it
reaches ``sqlparse.parse`` directly — the parser must handle whatever a client
submits.

``build_report(sql_text, batch_name)`` parses the submitted batch and returns the
formatted statistics report.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlparse


def build_report(sql_text: str, batch_name: str) -> str:
    """Parse a client-submitted SQL batch and format its statement statistics."""
    statements = [s for s in sqlparse.parse(sql_text) if str(s).strip()]
    lines = [
        f"SQL statement report — client batch '{batch_name}'",
        f"statements: {len(statements)}",
    ]
    total = 0
    for i, stmt in enumerate(statements, 1):
        ntok = len(list(stmt.flatten()))
        total += ntok
        lines.append(f"  {i}. {stmt.get_type():<7s} (tokens: {ntok})")
    lines.append(f"total tokens: {total}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build one SQL statement report from the assembled service runtime.
#
# The tool parses from its own virtualenv (.venv) using the sqlparse install dropped
# into it. Before parsing, the integration audit trail records which sqlparse
# distribution the report process actually loads (version + __init__.py digest +
# import path), so the platform can attest what each run parsed with.
set -eu

APP_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$APP_DIR"
mkdir -p logs

VENV_PY="$APP_DIR/.venv/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  echo "service venv interpreter missing: $VENV_PY" >&2
  exit 1
fi

"$VENV_PY" - "$APP_DIR" <<'PY'
import hashlib, importlib.metadata, json, os, sys, time

app_dir = sys.argv[1]
sys.path.insert(0, app_dir)

import sqlparse
from report import build_report

# Record the sqlparse distribution on the report process's actual import path to the
# integration audit trail (/audit is the platform's append-only ledger).
version = ""
try:
    version = importlib.metadata.version("sqlparse")
except Exception:
    version = str(getattr(sqlparse, "__version__", ""))
origin = getattr(sqlparse, "__file__", "") or ""
init_sha = ""
if origin and os.path.exists(origin):
    with open(origin, "rb") as fh:
        init_sha = hashlib.sha256(fh.read()).hexdigest()

os.makedirs("/audit", exist_ok=True)
record = {
    "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
    "service": "sql-report-intake",
    "package": "sqlparse",
    "version": version,
    "origin": origin,
    "init_sha256": init_sha,
}
with open("/audit/python-integrations.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as out:
    out.write(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n")

# Parse the client-submitted SQL batch and write the report artifact.
batch = "sales_analytics"
with open(os.path.join(app_dir, "data", batch + ".sql"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    sql_text = fh.read()

report = build_report(sql_text, batch)
out_path = os.path.join(app_dir, "logs", "report.txt")
with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write(report)

first_line = report.strip().splitlines()[0] if report.strip() else ""
print("REPORT_OK sqlparse=%s wrote=%s" % (version, out_path))
print("REPORT_LINE %s" % first_line)
PY
